key_insight: A cluster-based wrapper feature selection method can match standard sequential selection performance while cutting computation for renewable energy prediction.
engineering_relevance: This helps streamline solar and wind forecasting pipelines by automatically selecting useful input variables and reducing training cost.
method: Conducted two literature reviews on wind power curve modeling and photovoltaic power prediction.
Proposed Cluster-based Sequential Feature Selection (CSFS), a model-agnostic clustering-based wrapper method.
Compared CSFS against SFS, filter methods, and Random Forest feature importance.
evidence_signal: Across both evaluation use cases, CSFS achieved predictive performance comparable to SFS while reducing computational cost by an average of 21%.
watch_item: Results depend on the selected datasets and feature sets, so transferability to other renewable forecasting settings should be validated.
paper_title: Improving Wind and Solar Power Prediction with Efficient Wrapper-based Feature Selection: An Empirical Study
